title: Cardboard Gets Recycled. Most Plastic Doesn't. #shorts
summary: In the US, 96.5% of cardboard boxes were recycled in 2018, but only 8.7% of all plastics and about 29% of PET bottles (US EPA). A bale is only recycled once a buyer takes it.
sources: Corrugated boxes recycled at 96.5% in 2018; aluminum beverage cans 50.4% (670,000 tons); glass containers 31.3% (3.1 million tons); PET bottles and jars 29.1%; plastic containers and packaging 13.6% (US EPA, Containers and Packaging: Product-Specific Data, 2018 data): https://www.epa.gov/facts-and-figures-about-materials-waste-and-recycling/containers-and-packaging-product-specific

Plastics generation 35.7 million tons in 2018; about three million tons recycled, an 8.7 percent recycling rate; 27 million tons landfilled (US EPA, Plastics: Material-Specific Data): https://www.epa.gov/facts-and-figures-about-materials-waste-and-recycling/plastics-material-specific-data

How a material recovery facility sorts a blue cart: trucks unload, workers pre-sort plastic bags and hazardous items by hand, disc screens lift cardboard and flat paper, a glass breaker shatters glass so it falls through a screen and a cyclone lifts lighter paper and plastic off it, optical sorters with air jets, a magnet picks up tin cans, an eddy current 'acts like a magnet in reverse' and repels foil, cans and pie plates onto another belt, sorted material is baled and sold; '90% automated sorting by machines', 'the other 10% is handled manually'; 'garbage bags are never opened during the sorting process'; destinations: plastics to Canada, metal cans and foil to Eastern Canada, cardboard to Canada and the US, paper to Eastern Canada, the US, India, Malaysia and Taiwan, glass to Western Canada (City of Calgary, How the recycling facility works): https://www.calgary.ca/uep/wrs/recycling-information/residential-services/blue-cart-recycling/how-recycling-works.html

scenes.narration: {96.5%|Ninety-six and a half percent} of cardboard boxes in the US get recycled.
Plastic, every kind counted? {8.7%|Eight point seven percent}.
Even plastic bottles only reach about {29%|twenty-nine percent}.
The sorting plant can pull out both. Cameras spot them, and puffs of air knock them onto their own lines.
